scenario: MySQL 8.4.11 REPEATABLE-READ: loser transaction cannot see winner row via plain consistent read after duplicate-key upsert; only current read (FOR UPDATE) sees it

environment.transaction_isolation: REPEATABLE-READ (server default, asserted at probe start)
environment.note: container is a pre-existing sandbox from earlier 2026-09-29 evidence runs, reused for this read-only probe

table_under_probe: bpm_process_instance_idempotency (V118 DDL + V121 claim_token varchar(64) NULL DEFAULT NULL; unique key (tenant_id, process_definition_key, business_key))

steps.action: SET default isolation asserted; START TRANSACTION; plain SELECT COUNT(*)
INSERT (tenant_id=1, process_definition_key='leave', business_key='BK-1', claim_token='token-A') then COMMIT
plain consistent SELECT COUNT(*) after A committed
INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = LAST_INSERT_ID(id) with claim_token='token-B' (same as mapper insertOrLockUniqueKey)
steps.result: duplicate-key path taken; NO DuplicateKeyException surfaced

steps.action: plain consistent SELECT COUNT(*) after the duplicate-key upsert
SELECT COUNT(*), MAX(claim_token) ... FOR UPDATE (current read, same as V121 selectByUniqueKeyForUpdate)

conclusions: In REPEATABLE-READ, a transaction that took its snapshot before the winner committed cannot observe the winner row through a plain consistent read, even after its own duplicate-key upsert.

The mapper upsert INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = LAST_INSERT_ID(id) does NOT raise DuplicateKeyException on the duplicate path, so ownership cannot be decided from "no exception". With Connector/J default useAffectedRows=false the same statement returns affected rows 1 for the duplicate path, so ownership cannot be decided from affected rows either. Both old decision inputs are unsound.
Only a current read (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) sees the committed winner row and yields the real claim_token, which is what V121 + selectByUniqueKeyForUpdate implements.

Any V118-era code path doing a plain consistency read after the upsert would return no row and fail-closed as PROCESS_INSTANCE_IDEMPOTENCY_PENDING even though a valid instance already exists; this matches the preserved historical failure reproduction bpm-idempotency-real-chain-20260929_121828.json (1 success / 9 PENDING).
not_covered: physical master/replica, real read-write splitting, multi-tenant physical connections
production-scale concurrency, lock wait, deadlock/recovery behaviour
actual BPM service-chain behaviour (this is a SQL-level isolation probe, not the application path)
